problem_statement: matsuzaka-yuki/Mizuki is a production Astro 6 blog theme (Svelte islands, Tailwind v4, MDX content, an interactive archive with a client-only ArchivePanel that filters posts by tag and category from the URL query string). Readers land on a flat, year-grouped archive with only a small category pill bar for navigation, so a first-time reader has no curated entry point into the journal. The PRD asks you to extend the reading experience with a site-wide 'Reading paths' discovery bench, rendered once by the shared grid layout so it appears on every reading surface (home, archive, post detail, about, projects). The bench is a card-base panel with a row of tappable reading-path chips (Start here, Deep dives, Quick reads, By topic, Fresh from the studio) that each route to a tag-filtered archive view via the theme's existing getTagUrl mechanism, plus a 'Now reading for' focus readout and a Switch focus control that flips the bench between long reads and quick reads and keeps the readout in sync. A previous revision shipped this bench but (a) pinned the chip row to a fixed-width no-wrap track that overflows a 390px phone horizontally, (b) styled it as a plain gray slab instead of the theme's card-base surface, and (c) only rendered it on the home page. Rework the reading-path bench so it: lays out responsively with no horizontal overflow on mobile; keeps the Mizuki card-base surface and primary-accent styling; renders consistently across home, archive, post detail and about; and keeps the Switch focus control wired so the readout always reflects the active focus after a click. Keep the chips, their labels, their tag-filter destinations, and the archive interaction model exactly as shipped; the fix must live in the reading-path bench component's own file.
required_content: The site-wide reading-path discovery bench renders on home, archive, post detail and about with all five reading-path chips (Start here, Deep dives, Quick reads, By topic, Fresh from the studio) and their descriptive hints.
Each reading-path chip remains a link into a tag-filtered archive view, preserving the theme's existing getTagUrl tag-filter interaction model.
On a 390px mobile view the reading-path row lays out without any horizontal document overflow (no horizontal scrollbar).
The bench keeps the Mizuki card-base surface styling, rounded chips, primary-color accent heading, and 'Reading paths' title, matching the surrounding chrome.
The 'Switch focus' control flips the bench between long reads and quick reads and re-syncs the 'Now reading for' readout so it reflects the active focus after each click.
design_constraints: Preserve the Mizuki design language: card-base surfaces, rounded chips, the theme's spacing rhythm, primary-color accents, and the existing archive category bar and post list.
Keep the reading-path chips' content, labels, hint text, and tag-filter destinations identical; only the bench's responsive layout, surface styling, cross-page presence and focus wiring may change.
The change must live in the reading-path bench component's own file; do not alter the ArchivePanel, the category bar, the post list, url-utils, or other routes' bodies.
The reading-path row must wrap or otherwise reflow so a 390px viewport shows no horizontal overflow, while the desktop and tablet layouts stay visually stable.
Do not introduce external stock imagery, remote fonts, analytics, or network calls; every page must stay runtime-clean (no console or network errors).
state_constraints: desktop_bench_home and desktop_archive capture the reading-path bench at 1440px, where the bench sits above the page content on the card-base surface and lays out without overflow on every leg.

mobile_bench_home and mobile_archive capture the bench at 390px: on the shipped (defective) revision the fixed-width no-wrap reading-path row pushes the document past the viewport, causing a horizontal-scroll defect that the fix must remove.

desktop_bench_home, desktop_archive, desktop_post_detail and desktop_about all carry the shared reading-path bench in the reference; the bench must be present on each of these routes (cross-page consistency).
reading_focus_toggle clicks the Switch focus control on the home bench; after the click the 'Now reading for' readout must read 'quick reads' (the readout re-syncs to the active focus).
Source inspection confirms the archive mounts a client-only ArchivePanel Svelte island fed by tag/category query params, and the reading-path bench reuses that tag-filter mechanism via getTagUrl.

change_completion: The reading-path discovery bench renders across home, archive, post detail and about with all five chips and their hints.
Each chip still links into a tag-filtered archive view (getTagUrl interaction model preserved), and the Switch focus control re-syncs the readout after a click.
The mobile reading-path view shows no horizontal overflow after the fix.
design_consistency: The bench keeps the card-base surface, rounded chips, and primary-accent heading of the surrounding chrome on every route.
Desktop and tablet layouts stay visually stable; only the mobile reflow changes.
regression: The archive category bar, the year-grouped post list, and the home/post/projects/about routes remain reachable and unchanged.
Every page stays runtime-clean with no console or network errors.
responsive: 390px mobile reading-path bench has no horizontal document overflow.
The reading-path chips wrap intentionally on narrow viewports rather than forcing a fixed-width horizontal track.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro 6 (Mizuki blog theme) extend_interaction task, hardened to L4. The reference ships a responsive, card-base 'Reading paths' discovery bench rendered site-wide by the shared MainGridLayout, with a wired Switch-focus control. Content and DOM are byte-identical across the reference, the shipped-with-defect baseline and a shallow non-fix bad solution; only the reading-path bench component's file differs. The bad solution fails four orthogonal product gates: no_horizontal_overflow (mobile chip-row overflow), visual_regression (off-palette dark-teal slab vs the light card-base surface), cross-page dom_assertions (bench missing on post detail and about), and interaction_assertions (Switch focus click succeeds but the readout stays stale). The baseline reproduces the original three layout/visual/presence defects but keeps the focus wiring correct, so it fails the first three gates and passes the interaction gate. Product-grade gates: enforce_console_errors (max 0), cross-page DOM assertions, visual_regression on in-viewport bench states, and an interaction-trajectory terminal-state assertion.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Mizuki is a runnable Astro 6 blog theme with an interactive tag/category archive filter; extend_interaction adds a responsive, site-wide reading-path discovery bench that reuses that tag-filter model, anchored on four orthogonal product gates (overflow, visual, cross-page presence, interaction terminal state).
